format.summary: A planeswalker-centric set built around Empower Jace, which creates or grows a Jace token that can minus one to surveil or minus three to draw. There are ten supported archetypes: the allied pairs are Hexhaven schools and the enemy pairs are planeswalker themes. The rares are full of pushed bombs plus interesting build-arounds, and the hosts called it a breath of fresh air.
format.speed: Not directly assessed yet since they had only played early access; it has plenty of aggressive archetypes alongside ramp and graveyard control.

colors.take: Deep in powerful rares like Garruk, Simulacrum Shaper and Hungering Puppetbeast, with well-supported ramp for heavy green cards.
Very strong rares, including multiple Jaces, Lyra, the Sphinx and Seasoned Cryomancer.
Good removal and bombs such as Lich's Relic, Garruk and Overwrite the Multiverse, plus self-mill support.
Two A-level planeswalkers, Chandra and Ajani Unrelenting, along with aggressive creatures.
Many cards lean on life gain, which makes some rares like Ajani Resolute traps outside that deck.

pairs.take: Fatehold surveil and scry aggro; surveil triggers come naturally, powering cards like Proctor and Denzilore.
Graveyard-math self-mill control and midrange with threshold (seven cards in the graveyard) payoffs.
Stingerquill aggro that cares about dealing non-combat damage to the opponent, using lots of one-mana pings.
Konstrari ramp using Heartwood mana tokens into big six- and seven-drops; well suited to payoffs like Verdant Kraken.
Vigorbloom life gain, where creatures grow when you gain life.
Liliana's grindy attrition midrange with graveyard, sacrifice and token themes.
Chandra's prowess with noncreature spells, presumably aggressive.
Garruk's bestiary, combining deathtouch and trample with payoffs for big creatures.
Ajani's aggressive army with a light +1/+1 counter theme.
Jace's mastery, the home of Empower Jace and the Way enchantment cycle, possibly stretching to five colors.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: Creates or adds loyalty to a Jace token; at three you usually cash it in for a card, and opponents must decide whether to attack small Jaces. Most removal can hit planeswalkers.

mechanics.name: Prepared
mechanics.take: Creatures enter with an attached cheap spell, giving you extra value; entering prepared isn't a trigger, so Karn, Argent Defender doesn't stop it.

mechanics.name: Threshold / self-mill
mechanics.take: Blue-black mills itself with one-mana prepared spells to reach seven cards in the graveyard.

mechanics.name: Heartwood tokens
mechanics.take: Artifact tokens that tap for red or green, fueling ramp and artifact sacrifice synergies.

mechanics.name: Ways
mechanics.take: A five-color enchantment cycle that gives Jace tokens extra abilities.

advice: Don't take Ajani Resolute or Germinate Recruits and then force life gain; they only improve an already good life gain deck.
Mono or heavy green makes Hexhaven Invigorator great, but in an even two-color split it effectively costs six or more.
Avoid tapping out to pay five for Lyra, Tolarian Archangel's ability into open removal.
With Darklight Phoenix, prioritize Silence the Echo and cheap removal to trigger its return.
Play Vraska, the Cutting Glare on turn three if you can rather than holding it for six lands.
Avoid cute tutors and planeswalker-matters cards like Loyal Tutor and Entrust the Spark.
Bonus-sheet combo: Splinter Twin plus the common Divining Duelist goes infinite.
